the odds ratio for postmenopausal breast cancer is not significantly different from 1.0, and that the odds ratio is not affected by the patient's clinical indication for estrogen therapy or the reason for mammography.

the odds ratios for the association of breast cancer and estrogen use vary from 0.3 to 2.3, depending on the clinical features of the patients, and that the clinical characteristics of breast cancer patients are often different from those of the comparison patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical phenomena that influence the association between estrogens and cancer, rather than with the question of whether estrogens are causally related to the development of breast cancer.
the clinical characteristics of patients who are exposed to estrogens, rather than with the chemical effects of estrogens per se.
the clinical phenomena that affect the interpretation of epidemiological data.
